body: I see this too on latest canary locally on one of my projects. In fact if I open a new clean repro example in StackBlitz https://stackblitz.com/fork/github/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/reproduction-template-app-dir then it reproduces immediately. Though I can't immediately reproduce on the blank template when running the same locally…

On StackBlitz it appears that react-dom-server.edge.development.js's `require('react-dom')` from app-router.tsx is resolving to version 18.2.0, instead of the bundled canary ("next") version. Hopefully #48896 will fix as it changes how the imports work?
Thanks @sophiebits for the pointers! I'm wondering if the require hook is affected by how Stackblitz runs (e.g. causing ordering differences)...

I got the same problem.

I have vafried this issue still exists in latest 13.3.2 version published hours ago. What's interesting is that it's not working on my local machine after I start built project, but it's working well when I deploy it to vercel.

I hope this issue could be fixed.

The problem seems to be related to workers being disable when running on StackBlitz - but I'm not sure about other cases.

issue.title: Fix `next dev` failing for app when `__NEXT_DISABLE_MEMORY_WATCHER` is set
issue.body:
This env should only affect the teardown & restart process, instead of the `useWorkers` option. This also solves the problem of running `next dev` on StackBlitz (which has the env var set: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/48964#issuecomment-1528569879).

Closes #48964.

body: @pierrechevaliercf try 13.4.0. If you're doing a custom request handler + standalone + appdir, you'll need to set `process.env.__NEXT_PRIVATE_PREBUNDLED_REACT = "next"` or else it'll try to load the experimental react-dom

issue.title: dev(next): adopt fix for next issue 48964
